issues.legal_issue: A contemporaneous tape recording of a relevant conversation is admissible when its recording and integrity are adequately proved.
material_facts: A concealed microphone and tape recorder captured a conversation during which a bribe was offered and handed over.
A competent witness proved how the recording was made, and the speakers’ voices were identified.
Although the tape was not sealed, other evidence supported that it had not been tampered with, and the defence did not suggest that it had been altered.
The dialogue was proved by the recipient of the bribe, and the recording corroborated that witness’s testimony.
issues.conclusion: The dialogue was relevant as part of the res gestae, and the tape recording was admissible and could corroborate the witness’s testimony. The court must receive tape evidence cautiously and be satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that it has not been tampered with; the recording met that standard here.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 7 and 8 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, a contemporaneous record of a relevant event or conversation may itself be a relevant fact, and a contemporaneous dialogue may form part of the res gestae. The court approved Rup Chand v. Mahabir Parshad and Mahindra Nath v. Biswanath Kundu, and followed S. Pratap Singh v. State of Punjab and R. v. Maqsud Ali. Because magnetic recording can be erased and reused, the time, place, accuracy, and identification of voices must be proved, and the court must be satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the recording was not tampered with.

rule.if: criminal_evidence_proceeding and conversation_relevant_to_offence and contemporaneous_conversation_recorded and recording_method_proved_by_competent_witness and speakers_identified and recording_integrity_proved_beyond_reasonable_doubt

predicates.criminal_evidence_proceeding: The recording is offered as evidence in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.conversation_relevant_to_offence: The recorded conversation concerns an event relevant to the alleged offence.
predicates.contemporaneous_conversation_recorded: A recording device captured the conversation as it occurred.
predicates.recording_method_proved_by_competent_wit: A competent witness explained when, where, and how the recording was made and reproduced.
predicates.speakers_identified: A witness identified the voices recorded.
predicates.recording_integrity_proved_beyond_reason: The evidence satisfies the court beyond reasonable doubt that the recording was not altered or tampered with.

issues.definition: When a relevant conversation is recorded during a criminal proceeding and the recording method, speakers, and integrity are established, the recording is admissible.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory restriction on using statements made to police during an investigation does not exclude a private conversation with a decoy when the speaker does not address a police officer.
material_facts: An investigation into an alleged bribe was underway when the conversation occurred.
A decoy assisted the investigation and spoke with the accused, while police officers listened from another room.
The accused did not know that police officers were listening, and neither participant addressed a police officer.
issues.conclusion: The conversation was not barred by section 162 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, because neither participant made a statement to a police officer.
issues.legal_principle: Section 162 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, did not apply because the accused and the decoy spoke to each other, not to a police officer. The court distinguished Ramkishan Mithanlal Sharma v. State of Bombay, where statements made during an identification procedure directed and supervised by police could be regarded as statements to police officers.

rule.if: criminal_trial and police_investigation_underway and conversation_between_private_participants and decoy_assisting_investigation and police_officers_not_addressed_or_participating

predicates.criminal_trial: The conversation is offered in a criminal trial.
predicates.police_investigation_underway: A police investigation was in progress when the conversation took place.
predicates.conversation_between_private_participant: The accused and another person spoke directly to one another rather than addressing a police officer.
predicates.decoy_assisting_investigation: One participant was cooperating with police as a decoy.
predicates.police_officers_not_addressed_or_partici: Police officers were not spoken to and did not take part in the conversation.

issues.definition: A conversation during an investigation is not excluded as a statement to police when the participants speak to each other and police officers are neither addressed nor involved in it.

issues.legal_issue: A voluntary incriminating conversation is not compelled self-incrimination merely because police secretly arranged and recorded it.
material_facts: The accused spoke with a decoy during a trap arranged by police and did not know police were listening or recording.
The accused was free to speak or remain silent, and the conversation was not extracted by force, duress, coercion, or oppressive means.
issues.conclusion: The accused was not compelled to be a witness against himself, and the secret recording alone did not make the conversation inadmissible under Article 20(3) of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Article 20(3) of the Constitution protects against compelled self-incrimination. Compulsion may arise from force, coercion, duress, or oppressive means of extracting a statement; a voluntary conversation is not rendered compelled merely because it was secretly recorded without the speaker’s knowledge.

rule.if: accused_in_criminal_proceeding and incriminating_conversation_recorded_without_knowledge and accused_free_to_speak_or_remain_silent and no_force_coercion_or_oppression

predicates.accused_in_criminal_proceeding: The person whose statement is used is accused in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.incriminating_conversation_recorded_with: The accused made an incriminating statement in a conversation that was recorded without the accused’s knowledge.
predicates.accused_free_to_speak_or_remain_silent: The accused was free to speak or not to speak.
predicates.no_force_coercion_or_oppression: No force, duress, coercion, or oppressive method was used to obtain the statement.

issues.definition: An accused’s secretly recorded statement is not protected as compelled self-incrimination when the accused was free to remain silent and the statement was not obtained by force, coercion, or oppression.

issues.legal_issue: The convictions for offering bribes were supported by the eyewitness testimony and its corroboration.
material_facts: The recipient of the bribes testified to an earlier offer and to a later offer and handover of money.
A municipal investigator witnessed and corroborated the earlier offer, and the courts found that investigator reliable and not an accomplice.
The tape recording corroborated the recipient’s testimony about the later conversation and offer.
The lower courts made concurrent findings that the charges were proved.
issues.legal_principle: The court accepted the lower courts’ assessment of the evidence: the earlier offer was corroborated by a reliable witness who was not an accomplice, and the later offer was corroborated by the admissible tape recording. It found no ground to disturb the concurrent findings of guilt.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_criminal_conviction and eyewitness_testimony_supports_bribe_offer and earlier_offer_independently_corroborated and later_offer_corroborated_by_admissible_recording and concurrent_findings_support_guilt

predicates.appeal_challenging_criminal_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.eyewitness_testimony_supports_bribe_offe: An eyewitness testified that the accused offered a bribe.
predicates.earlier_offer_independently_corroborated: A reliable witness who was not an accomplice independently corroborated an earlier offer.
predicates.later_offer_corroborated_by_admissible_r: An admissible recording corroborated the eyewitness account of a later offer.
predicates.concurrent_findings_support_guilt: The lower courts made concurrent findings that the evidence established guilt.

issues.definition: A conviction is upheld on appeal when eyewitness evidence of bribe offers is corroborated and the lower courts’ concurrent findings support guilt.

issues.legal_issue: Mitigating personal circumstances may justify reducing the substantive sentence in an appeal from a conviction.
material_facts: The appellant was sixty years old and suffered from cardiac problems.
He had been taken from hospital to jail and had remained in custody before being released on bail.
The court considered these and other circumstances when reviewing the sentence.
issues.conclusion: The court reduced the substantive term of imprisonment to the period already undergone and dismissed the appeal with that modification.
issues.legal_principle: The court exercised its sentencing discretion in light of the appellant’s age, cardiac illness, custody, and other circumstances; it cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this reduction.

predicates.appeal_includes_sentence_review: The appeal places the substantive sentence before the court for review.
predicates.offender_has_significant_health_or_age_m: The offender has significant mitigating circumstances relating to age or health.
predicates.offender_has_already_served_part_of_sent: The offender has already spent time in custody serving the sentence.

issues.definition: When an appeal includes sentence review and significant age or health mitigation exists alongside time already served, the substantive imprisonment is reduced.
